blocking: The Weddings page promises family-led planning but repeatedly presents specific participants and ritual sequences as defaults. That inconsistency needs correction before cultural fluency earns launch sign-off.

fixes.where: weddings.html — Sofreh Aghd, Haldi & Pheras, Anand Karaj
fixes.what: Make the detailed sequences conditional within each section: 'For the rituals you choose, we confirm the order and participants with you and your officiant.' Replace prescribed fathers, parents and married women with the participants the couple names; retain specific traditions as optional examples.
fixes.why: The introductory qualification does not fully counter later assumptions about family structure and observance.

fixes.what: Replace 'the mahr as the families have agreed it' with 'the mahr as agreed by the couple and confirmed with their officiant'; describe family participation separately.
fixes.why: The current wording gives families ownership of a decision that should explicitly center the couple.

fixes.what: Keep two short sentences of coordination work visible per ceremony; move the long lists of ritual cues into the existing 'Details we confirm with your family' disclosures.
fixes.why: Parents and couples should quickly understand the help being offered without reading a ceremony manual.

fixes.where: how-we-work.html — Full planning scope and FAQ
fixes.what: Replace 'every wedding day run' with 'the wedding events agreed in your proposal'; make the FAQ use the same scope.
fixes.why: The prominent promise currently sounds broader than the event, staffing and hour limits explained below.

fixes.what: Move the existing Call / WhatsApp line directly above the form, below the heading divider.
fixes.why: Parents who prefer speaking should see that route before working through the form, especially on phones.
